# Add frame level operations to enhanced multi-frame instances

An enhanced multi-frame instance describes each frame with functional groups, shared or per frame.

Add a `pydicom.multiframe` module, the same objects also reachable from `pydicom`, holding `frame_attributes(ds, index)`, `varying_attributes(ds)`, `extract_frames(ds, indices)`, `merge_frames(datasets)`, `group_frames(ds, keys)`, `sort_frames(ds, keys)` and `MultiFrameError`. All six functions check what they are given the same way first. `MultiFrameError`, a `ValueError`, is raised for a dataset with no per-frame groups, empty counting as none, transfer syntax, SOP class or instance UID, not exactly one pixel data element, a shared group sequence present but not holding one item, a frame count absent or disagreeing with them, pixel data too short or malformed for them, a missing frame, an empty or repeating selection, no keys, a key that is not an attribute name or tag, incomparable values, and uncombinable inputs.

`frame_attributes` returns the attributes inside the macros applying to one zero-based frame, the shared macros written first and the frame's own second, a per-frame macro replacing the shared macro carrying its tag. It is a copy, changing it leaves the instance alone. `varying_attributes` returns the tags whose effective value is not the same for every frame, nothing for one frame.

The other four derive new instances. `extract_frames` keeps the frames `indices` names, in that order. `merge_frames` takes every frame of its inputs, one or more, which must agree on SOP class, transfer syntax, pixel data element and image pixel attributes. `group_frames` returns a list of one instance per distinct combination of the effective values of `keys`, in first-appearance order, each keeping its old order, frames carrying none of it grouping together, even when that is every frame. `sort_frames` puts them in ascending order of those values, first key first, missing values last, ties as they were.

A derived instance carries one shared group. In-stack positions are renumbered from one within each stack, in frame order, among the frames carrying them. Among the frames carrying index values, a dimension every one of them reaches with one value is then dropped, from the dimension index description and from those frames; one they do not all reach is kept. An emptied one is removed, description included, not left empty. What remains is renumbered, each alone, to 1, 2, 3 in first-seen order. Only then is a macro with the same value for every frame stored once, in the shared group, every other in each frame's own. Its pixel data element is rebuilt in the new frame order, encapsulated again if it was, padded to an even length if not, any extended offset table dropped. It takes a new SOP instance UID, its file meta naming that and its SOP class, and a source image sequence holding one item per input, in input order, naming its SOP class, SOP instance UID and the 1-based numbers of frames taken from it, in result order. Whatever else it carries comes from the first input, copied. Inputs are unchanged and share nothing with the result.

Implemented enhanced multiframe operations in [multiframe.py](/app/src/pydicom/multiframe.py), exported through [pydicom/__init__.py](/app/src/pydicom/__init__.py), with focused tests in [test_multiframe.py](/app/tests/test_multiframe.py).

Validation and targeted tests pass: 222 passed, 3 skipped. The full suite reached 682 passed before an unrelated TLS certificate failure while downloading external test data.

const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /app/src/pydicom/multiframe.py
+"""Operations on enhanced multi-frame image instances.
+
+The functions in this module operate on the functional groups that describe
+the frames of an enhanced multi-frame image.  They deliberately work on the
+encoded pixel data rather than decoding and re-encoding it, so compressed
+frames can be selected and reordered without requiring a pixel data plugin.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import copy
+import math
+import operator
+from collections.abc import Iterable
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from functools import cmp_to_key
+from numbers import Integral
+from struct import unpack_from
+from typing import Any, NoReturn
+
+from pydicom.dataelem import DataElement
+from pydicom.datadict import tag_for_keyword
+from pydicom.dataset import Dataset
+from pydicom.encaps import encapsulate
+from pydicom.pixels.utils import concatenate_packed_frames, get_packed_frame
+from pydicom.sequence import Sequence
+from pydicom.tag import BaseTag, Tag
+from pydicom.uid import UID, generate_uid
+
+
+class MultiFrameError(ValueError):
+    """Raised when a multi-frame instance cannot be operated on."""
+
+
+# Functional group and frame-level tags
+_SHARED_FUNCTIONAL_GROUPS = Tag(0x52009229)
+_PER_FRAME_FUNCTIONAL_GROUPS = Tag(0x52009230)
+_NUMBER_OF_FRAMES = Tag(0x00280008)
+_SOP_CLASS_UID = Tag(0x00080016)
+_SOP_INSTANCE_UID = Tag(0x00080018)
+_TRANSFER_SYNTAX_UID = Tag(0x00020010)
+_SOURCE_IMAGE_SEQUENCE = Tag(0x00082112)
+_REFERENCED_SOP_CLASS_UID = Tag(0x00081150)
+_REFERENCED_SOP_INSTANCE_UID = Tag(0x00081155)
+_REFERENCED_FRAME_NUMBER = Tag(0x00081160)
+_DIMENSION_INDEX_SEQUENCE = Tag(0x00209222)
+_DIMENSION_INDEX_VALUES = Tag(0x00209157)
+_STACK_ID = Tag(0x00209056)
+_IN_STACK_POSITION_NUMBER = Tag(0x00209057)
+_EXTENDED_OFFSET_TABLE = Tag(0x7FE00001)
+_EXTENDED_OFFSET_TABLE_LENGTHS = Tag(0x7FE00002)
+_PHOTOMETRIC_INTERPRETATION = Tag(0x00280004)
+
+_PIXEL_DATA_TAGS = (
+    Tag(0x7FE00008),  # Float Pixel Data
+    Tag(0x7FE00009),  # Double Float Pixel Data
+    Tag(0x7FE00010),  # Pixel Data
+)
+
+# The image pixel attributes which determine the shape and interpretation of
+# native and encapsulated frames. Number of Frames is intentionally excluded:
+# it is expected to differ between inputs to merge_frames().
+_IMAGE_PIXEL_ATTRIBUTES = (
+    Tag(0x00280002),  # Samples Per Pixel
+    _PHOTOMETRIC_INTERPRETATION,
+    Tag(0x00280006),  # Planar Configuration
+    Tag(0x00280010),  # Rows
+    Tag(0x00280011),  # Columns
+    Tag(0x00280100),  # Bits Allocated
+    Tag(0x00280101),  # Bits Stored
+    Tag(0x00280102),  # High Bit
+    Tag(0x00280103),  # Pixel Representation
+)
+
+_MISSING = object()
+
+
+@dataclass
+class _ValidatedDataset:
+    dataset: Dataset
+    number_of_frames: int
+    transfer_syntax: UID
+    encapsulated: bool
+    pixel_tag: BaseTag
+    pixel_vr: str
+    frames: tuple[bytes, ...]
+    native_frame_length: int | None
+    native_frame_pixels: int | None
+    native_bits_allocated: int | None
+    shared_macros: dict[BaseTag, DataElement]
+    per_frame_macros: tuple[dict[BaseTag, DataElement], ...]
+    sop_class_uid: Any
+    sop_instance_uid: Any
+
+
+@dataclass
+class _FrameState:
+    source: _ValidatedDataset
+    index: int
+    macros: dict[BaseTag, DataElement]
+
+
+def _error(message: str) -> NoReturn:
+    raise MultiFrameError(message)
+
+
+def _element_value(element: Any) -> Any:
+    """Return an element value, converting raw elements if necessary."""
+
+    if element is None:
+        return None
+    return element.value
+
+
+def _is_empty(value: Any) -> bool:
+    if value is None:
+        return True
+    if isinstance(value, str | bytes | bytearray):
+        return len(value) == 0
+    return False
+
+
+def _as_positive_int(value: Any, name: str) -> int:
+    if isinstance(value, bool):
+        _error(f"{name} must be a positive integer")
+
+    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
+        if len(value) != 1:
+            _error(f"{name} must have one value")
+        value = value[0]
+
+    try:
+        result = operator.index(value)
+    except (TypeError, ValueError):
+        if isinstance(value, str):
+            try:
+                result = int(value.strip())
+            except (TypeError, ValueError):
+                _error(f"{name} must be a positive integer")
+        else:
+            _error(f"{name} must be a positive integer")
+
+    if result <= 0:
+        _error(f"{name} must be a positive integer")
+
+    return result
+
+
+def _as_bytes(value: Any, description: str) -> bytes:
+    if isinstance(value, bytes):
+        return value
+    if isinstance(value, (bytearray, memoryview)):
+        return bytes(value)
+
+    # EncapsulatedBuffer and other readable buffers are commonly used for
+    # compressed Pixel Data. Preserve their current position while materialising
+    # the data for validation and frame selection.
+    if hasattr(value, "read") and hasattr(value, "seek"):
+        try:
+            position = value.tell() if hasattr(value, "tell") else 0
+            value.seek(0)
+            data = value.read()
+            value.seek(position)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            raise MultiFrameError(f"Unable to read {description}") from exc
+        if isinstance(data, bytes):
+            return data
+        try:
+            return bytes(data)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            raise MultiFrameError(f"Unable to read {description}") from exc
+
+    try:
+        return bytes(value)
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError(f"{description} is not byte data") from exc
+
+
+def _parse_functional_group_item(item: Any, description: str) -> dict[BaseTag, DataElement]:
+    if not isinstance(item, Dataset):
+        _error(f"{description} must contain Dataset items")
+
+    macros: dict[BaseTag, DataElement] = {}
+    try:
+        elements = list(item.elements())
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError(f"Unable to read {description}") from exc
+
+    for element in elements:
+        if element.VR != "SQ":
+            _error(f"{description} contains a non-sequence functional group")
+
+        try:
+            values = element.value
+            if len(values) != 1 or not isinstance(values[0], Dataset):
+                _error(
+                    f"The functional group macro {element.tag} in {description} "
+                    "must contain one item"
+                )
+        except MultiFrameError:
+            raise
+        except Exception as exc:
+            raise MultiFrameError(
+                f"The functional group macro {element.tag} is malformed"
+            ) from exc
+
+        macros[element.tag] = element
+
+    return macros
+
+
+def _get_group_items(ds: Dataset) -> tuple[Dataset | None, tuple[Dataset, ...]]:
+    shared_element = ds.get(_SHARED_FUNCTIONAL_GROUPS)
+    shared_item: Dataset | None = None
+    if shared_element is not None:
+        try:
+            values = shared_element.value
+            if len(values) != 1 or not isinstance(values[0], Dataset):
+                _error(
+                    "Shared Functional Groups Sequence must contain exactly one item"
+                )
+            shared_item = values[0]
+        except MultiFrameError:
+            raise
+        except Exception as exc:
+            raise MultiFrameError(
+                "Shared Functional Groups Sequence is malformed"
+            ) from exc
+
+    per_frame_element = ds.get(_PER_FRAME_FUNCTIONAL_GROUPS)
+    if per_frame_element is None:
+        _error("Per-Frame Functional Groups Sequence is missing")
+
+    try:
+        per_frame_values = per_frame_element.value
+        if len(per_frame_values) == 0:
+            _error("Per-Frame Functional Groups Sequence is empty")
+        if not all(isinstance(item, Dataset) for item in per_frame_values):
+            _error("Per-Frame Functional Groups Sequence must contain Datasets")
+    except MultiFrameError:
+        raise
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError(
+            "Per-Frame Functional Groups Sequence is malformed"
+        ) from exc
+
+    return shared_item, tuple(per_frame_values)
+
+
+def _decode_offset_table(element: DataElement, name: str) -> list[int]:
+    value = element.value
+    if isinstance(value, (bytes, bytearray, memoryview)):
+        raw = bytes(value)
+        if len(raw) % 8:
+            _error(f"{name} is malformed")
+        return [unpack_from("<Q", raw, offset)[0] for offset in range(0, len(raw), 8)]
+
+    if value is None:
+        _error(f"{name} is malformed")
+
+    if isinstance(value, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(value, Iterable):
+        values = [value]
+    else:
+        values = list(value)
+
+    decoded: list[int] = []
+    for item in values:
+        if isinstance(item, bool):
+            _error(f"{name} is malformed")
+        try:
+            number = operator.index(item)
+        except (TypeError, ValueError):
+            _error(f"{name} is malformed")
+        if number < 0:
+            _error(f"{name} is malformed")
+        decoded.append(number)
+
+    return decoded
+
+
+def _extended_offsets(ds: Dataset) -> tuple[list[int], list[int]] | None:
+    offsets_element = ds.get(_EXTENDED_OFFSET_TABLE)
+    lengths_element = ds.get(_EXTENDED_OFFSET_TABLE_LENGTHS)
+    if offsets_element is None and lengths_element is None:
+        return None
+    if offsets_element is None or lengths_element is None:
+        _error("The Extended Offset Table and its lengths must be paired")
+
+    offsets = _decode_offset_table(offsets_element, "Extended Offset Table")
+    lengths = _decode_offset_table(lengths_element, "Extended Offset Table Lengths")
+    if not offsets or len(offsets) != len(lengths):
+        _error("The Extended Offset Table is malformed")
+    return offsets, lengths
+
+
+def _encapsulated_frames(
+    data: bytes,
+    number_of_frames: int,
+    extended_offsets: tuple[list[int], list[int]] | None,
+) -> tuple[bytes, ...]:
+    """Parse encapsulated Pixel Data and return one byte string per frame."""
+
+    if len(data) < 8:
+        _error("Encapsulated Pixel Data is too short")
+
+    try:
+        first_tag = unpack_from("<I", data, 0)[0]
+        bot_length = unpack_from("<I", data, 4)[0]
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError("Encapsulated Pixel Data is malformed") from exc
+
+    if first_tag != 0xFFFEE000 or bot_length % 4:
+        _error("Encapsulated Pixel Data has a malformed Basic Offset Table")
+
+    content_start = 8 + bot_length
+    if content_start > len(data):
+        _error("Encapsulated Pixel Data is too short for its Basic Offset Table")
+
+    bot_offsets = [
+        unpack_from("<I", data, offset)[0]
+        for offset in range(8, content_start, 4)
+    ]
+
+    # (offset from the first fragment item, fragment value)
+    fragments: list[tuple[int, bytes]] = []
+    position = content_start
+    delimiter_found = False
+    while position < len(data):
+        if position + 8 > len(data):
+            _error("Encapsulated Pixel Data ends in a partial item")
+
+        tag = unpack_from("<I", data, position)[0]
+        length = unpack_from("<I", data, position + 4)[0]
+        if tag == 0xFFFEE0DD:
+            if length != 0:
+                _error("The encapsulated sequence delimiter is malformed")
+            position += 8
+            delimiter_found = True
+            break
+
+        if tag != 0xFFFEE000 or length == 0xFFFFFFFF:
+            _error("Encapsulated Pixel Data contains a malformed fragment")
+        if length % 2:
+            _error("Encapsulated Pixel Data contains an odd-length fragment")
+
+        value_start = position + 8
+        value_end = value_start + length
+        if value_end > len(data):
+            _error("Encapsulated Pixel Data ends in a partial fragment")
+
+        fragments.append((position - content_start, data[value_start:value_end]))
+        position = value_end
+
+    if delimiter_found and position != len(data):
+        _error("Data follows the encapsulated sequence delimiter")
+    if not fragments:
+        _error("Encapsulated Pixel Data contains no frame fragments")
+
+    fragment_data_end = position - content_start
+    fragment_offsets = [offset for offset, _ in fragments]
+    offset_to_index = {offset: index for index, offset in enumerate(fragment_offsets)}
+
+    if extended_offsets is not None:
+        offsets, lengths = extended_offsets
+        if len(offsets) != number_of_frames or len(lengths) != number_of_frames:
+            _error("The Extended Offset Table disagrees with Number of Frames")
+        if offsets != sorted(offsets) or len(set(offsets)) != len(offsets):
+            _error("The Extended Offset Table is malformed")
+
+        frames: list[bytes] = []
+        for offset, length in zip(offsets, lengths):
+            if offset not in offset_to_index or length == 0:
+                _error("The Extended Offset Table is malformed")
+            fragment = fragments[offset_to_index[offset]][1]
+            if length > len(fragment):
+                _error("The Extended Offset Table is longer than its fragment")
+            frames.append(fragment[:length])
+        return tuple(frames)
+
+    if bot_offsets:
+        if len(bot_offsets) != number_of_frames:
+            _error("The Basic Offset Table disagrees with Number of Frames")
+        if bot_offsets != sorted(bot_offsets) or len(set(bot_offsets)) != len(bot_offsets):
+            _error("The Basic Offset Table is malformed")
+        if any(offset not in offset_to_index for offset in bot_offsets):
+            _error("The Basic Offset Table points to a missing fragment")
+
+        frames = []
+        for index, start in enumerate(bot_offsets):
+            start_index = offset_to_index[start]
+            end_index = (
+                offset_to_index[bot_offsets[index + 1]]
+                if index + 1 < len(bot_offsets)
+                else len(fragments)
+            )
+            if end_index <= start_index:
+                _error("The Basic Offset Table contains an empty frame")
+            frames.append(b"".join(value for _, value in fragments[start_index:end_index]))
+        return tuple(frames)
+
+    # With neither offset table present, one fragment per frame is unambiguous.
+    if len(fragments) == number_of_frames:
+        return tuple(value for _, value in fragments)
+    if number_of_frames == 1:
+        return (b"".join(value for _, value in fragments),)
+
+    # JPEG-family codestreams commonly carry multiple fragments per frame and
+    # can be split using their EOI marker when no offset table is available.
+    frames = []
+    current: list[bytes] = []
+    for _, fragment in fragments:
+        current.append(fragment)
+        if b"\xff\xd9" in fragment[-10:]:
+            frames.append(b"".join(current))
+            current = []
+    if current:
+        frames.append(b"".join(current))
+
+    if len(frames) != number_of_frames:
+        _error("Encapsulated Pixel Data does not contain the expected frames")
+    return tuple(frames)
+
+
+def _native_frames(
+    ds: Dataset,
+    pixel_tag: BaseTag,
+    number_of_frames: int,
+) -> tuple[tuple[bytes, ...], int, int | None, int]:
+    pixel_element = ds[pixel_tag]
+    data = _as_bytes(pixel_element.value, "native Pixel Data")
+
+    rows_element = ds.get(Tag(0x00280010))
+    columns_element = ds.get(Tag(0x00280011))
+    samples_element = ds.get(Tag(0x00280002))
+    if rows_element is None or columns_element is None or samples_element is None:
+        _error("Native Pixel Data lacks required image pixel attributes")
+
+    rows = _as_positive_int(rows_element.value, "Rows")
+    columns = _as_positive_int(columns_element.value, "Columns")
+    samples = _as_positive_int(samples_element.value, "Samples Per Pixel")
+    pixels_per_frame = rows * columns * samples
+
+    if pixel_tag == _PIXEL_DATA_TAGS[0]:
+        bytes_per_sample = 4
+        bits_allocated = None
+    elif pixel_tag == _PIXEL_DATA_TAGS[1]:
+        bytes_per_sample = 8
+        bits_allocated = None
+    else:
+        bits_element = ds.get(Tag(0x00280100))
+        if bits_element is None:
+            _error("Pixel Data lacks Bits Allocated")
+        bits_allocated = _as_positive_int(bits_element.value, "Bits Allocated")
+        if bits_allocated != 1 and bits_allocated % 8:
+            _error("Bits Allocated is not a supported native pixel size")
+
+        if bits_allocated == 1:
+            expected_length = math.ceil(pixels_per_frame * number_of_frames / 8)
+            if len(data) == expected_length:
+                pass
+            elif len(data) == expected_length + 1 and expected_length % 2:
+                pass
+            else:
+                _error("Native Pixel Data has an invalid length")
+
+            try:
+                frames = tuple(
+                    get_packed_frame(
+                        data,
+                        index,
+                        pixels_per_frame,
+                        pad=False,
+                    )
+                    for index in range(number_of_frames)
+                )
+            except Exception as exc:
+                raise MultiFrameError("Native Pixel Data is too short") from exc
+            return frames, math.ceil(pixels_per_frame / 8), pixels_per_frame, bits_allocated
+
+        bytes_per_sample = bits_allocated // 8
+
+    photometric_element = ds.get(_PHOTOMETRIC_INTERPRETATION)
+    photometric = photometric_element.value if photometric_element is not None else None
+    if photometric == "YBR_FULL_422":
+        # The encoded representation has two bytes per pixel rather than
+        # three samples per pixel.
+        frame_length = rows * columns * 2 * bytes_per_sample
+    else:
+        frame_length = pixels_per_frame * bytes_per_sample
+
+    expected_length = frame_length * number_of_frames
+    if len(data) == expected_length:
+        pass
+    elif len(data) == expected_length + 1 and expected_length % 2:
+        pass
+    else:
+        _error("Native Pixel Data has an invalid length")
+
+    frames = tuple(
+        data[index * frame_length : (index + 1) * frame_length]
+        for index in range(number_of_frames)
+    )
+    return frames, frame_length, None, bits_allocated
+
+
+def _validate_dataset(ds: Any) -> _ValidatedDataset:
+    """Validate an enhanced multi-frame dataset and collect frame data."""
+
+    if not isinstance(ds, Dataset):
+        _error("Expected a pydicom Dataset")
+
+    try:
+        shared_item, per_frame_items = _get_group_items(ds)
+
+        file_meta = getattr(ds, "file_meta", None)
+        if not isinstance(file_meta, Dataset):
+            _error("The dataset has no file meta information")
+        transfer_element = file_meta.get(_TRANSFER_SYNTAX_UID)
+        transfer_value = _element_value(transfer_element)
+        if _is_empty(transfer_value):
+            _error("Transfer Syntax UID is missing")
+        try:
+            transfer_syntax = UID(str(transfer_value))
+            if not transfer_syntax.is_transfer_syntax:
+                _error("Transfer Syntax UID is invalid")
+            encapsulated = transfer_syntax.is_encapsulated
+        except MultiFrameError:
+            raise
+        except Exception as exc:
+            raise MultiFrameError("Transfer Syntax UID is invalid") from exc
+
+        sop_class_element = ds.get(_SOP_CLASS_UID)
+        sop_instance_element = ds.get(_SOP_INSTANCE_UID)
+        sop_class_uid = _element_value(sop_class_element)
+        sop_instance_uid = _element_value(sop_instance_element)
+        if _is_empty(sop_class_uid):
+            _error("SOP Class UID is missing")
+        if _is_empty(sop_instance_uid):
+            _error("SOP Instance UID is missing")
+
+        pixel_tags = [tag for tag in _PIXEL_DATA_TAGS if tag in ds]
+        if len(pixel_tags) != 1:
+            _error("The dataset must contain exactly one pixel data element")
+        pixel_tag = pixel_tags[0]
+        pixel_element = ds[pixel_tag]
+
+        number_element = ds.get(_NUMBER_OF_FRAMES)
+        if number_element is None or _is_empty(_element_value(number_element)):
+            _error("Number of Frames is missing")
+        number_of_frames = _as_positive_int(number_element.value, "Number of Frames")
+        if number_of_frames != len(per_frame_items):
+            _error("Number of Frames disagrees with the Per-Frame Functional Groups")
+
+        shared_macros = (
+            {}
+            if shared_item is None
+            else _parse_functional_group_item(shared_item, "Shared Functional Groups")
+        )
+        per_frame_macros = tuple(
+            _parse_functional_group_item(item, "Per-Frame Functional Groups")
+            for item in per_frame_items
+        )
+
+        if encapsulated:
+            data = _as_bytes(pixel_element.value, "encapsulated Pixel Data")
+            frames = _encapsulated_frames(
+                data,
+                number_of_frames,
+                _extended_offsets(ds),
+            )
+            if len(frames) != number_of_frames:
+                _error("Encapsulated Pixel Data disagrees with Number of Frames")
+            native_frame_length = None
+            native_frame_pixels = None
+            native_bits_allocated = None
+        else:
+            (
+                frames,
+                native_frame_length,
+                native_frame_pixels,
+                native_bits_allocated,
+            ) = _native_frames(ds, pixel_tag, number_of_frames)
+
+        return _ValidatedDataset(
+            dataset=ds,
+            number_of_frames=number_of_frames,
+            transfer_syntax=transfer_syntax,
+            encapsulated=encapsulated,
+            pixel_tag=pixel_tag,
+            pixel_vr=pixel_element.VR,
+            frames=frames,
+            native_frame_length=native_frame_length,
+            native_frame_pixels=native_frame_pixels,
+            native_bits_allocated=native_bits_allocated,
+            shared_macros=shared_macros,
+            per_frame_macros=per_frame_macros,
+            sop_class_uid=sop_class_uid,
+            sop_instance_uid=sop_instance_uid,
+        )
+    except MultiFrameError:
+        raise
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError("The dataset is not a valid enhanced multi-frame instance") from exc
+
+
+def _copy_macro(element: DataElement) -> DataElement:
+    copied = copy.deepcopy(element)
+    copied.value = Sequence([copy.deepcopy(element.value[0])])
+    return copied
+
+
+def _effective_macros(info: _ValidatedDataset, index: int) -> dict[BaseTag, DataElement]:
+    macros = {tag: _copy_macro(element) for tag, element in info.shared_macros.items()}
+    macros.update(
+        {tag: _copy_macro(element) for tag, element in info.per_frame_macros[index].items()}
+    )
+    return macros
+
+
+def _flatten_macros(macros: dict[BaseTag, DataElement]) -> Dataset:
+    attributes = Dataset()
+    for element in macros.values():
+        item = element.value[0]
+        for attribute in item.elements():
+            attributes.add(copy.deepcopy(attribute))
+    return attributes
+
+
+def _frame_index(index: Any, number_of_frames: int) -> int:
+    if isinstance(index, bool):
+        _error("Frame index must be a zero-based integer")
+    try:
+        result = operator.index(index)
+    except (TypeError, ValueError):
+        _error("Frame index must be a zero-based integer")
+    if result < 0 or result >= number_of_frames:
+        _error("Frame index does not identify a frame")
+    return result
+
+
+def frame_attributes(ds: Dataset, index: int) -> Dataset:
+    """Return a copy of the effective functional-group attributes for a frame.
+
+    Shared functional group macros are applied first. A per-frame macro with
+    the same sequence tag replaces the shared macro.
+    """
+
+    info = _validate_dataset(ds)
+    frame = _frame_index(index, info.number_of_frames)
+    return _flatten_macros(_effective_macros(info, frame))
+
+
+def _values_equal(first: Any, second: Any) -> bool:
+    if first is _MISSING or second is _MISSING:
+        return first is second
+    if first is second:
+        return True
+
+    try:
+        result = first == second
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError("Frame attribute values cannot be compared") from exc
+
+    if isinstance(result, bool):
+        return result
+    try:
+        return bool(result)
+    except Exception:
+        try:
+            return bool(result.all())
+        except Exception as exc:
+            raise MultiFrameError("Frame attribute values cannot be compared") from exc
+
+
+def varying_attributes(ds: Dataset) -> set[BaseTag]:
+    """Return the functional-group attribute tags whose values vary by frame."""
+
+    info = _validate_dataset(ds)
+    if info.number_of_frames == 1:
+        return set()
+
+    attributes = [
+        _flatten_macros(_effective_macros(info, index))
+        for index in range(info.number_of_frames)
+    ]
+    tags: set[BaseTag] = set()
+    all_tags = set().union(*(set(dataset.keys()) for dataset in attributes))
+    for tag in all_tags:
+        first = attributes[0][tag].value if tag in attributes[0] else _MISSING
+        for dataset in attributes[1:]:
+            value = dataset[tag].value if tag in dataset else _MISSING
+            if not _values_equal(first, value):
+                tags.add(tag)
+                break
+    return tags
+
+
+def _normalise_keys(keys: Any) -> list[BaseTag]:
+    if keys is None:
+        _error("At least one frame attribute key is required")
+
+    if isinstance(keys, (str, BaseTag, Integral)):
+        raw_keys = [keys]
+    elif isinstance(keys, tuple) and len(keys) == 2 and all(
+        isinstance(value, Integral) and not isinstance(value, bool) for value in keys
+    ):
+        raw_keys = [keys]
+    else:
+        try:
+            raw_keys = list(keys)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            raise MultiFrameError("At least one frame attribute key is required") from exc
+
+    if not raw_keys:
+        _error("At least one frame attribute key is required")
+
+    output: list[BaseTag] = []
+    for key in raw_keys:
+        if isinstance(key, bool):
+            _error("A frame attribute key must be an attribute name or tag")
+        if isinstance(key, str):
+            tag = tag_for_keyword(key)
+            if tag is None:
+                try:
+                    tag = Tag(key)
+                except Exception as exc:
+                    raise MultiFrameError(
+                        f"'{key}' is not an attribute name or tag"
+                    ) from exc
+            output.append(Tag(tag))
+            continue
+
+        try:
+            output.append(Tag(key))
+        except Exception as exc:
+            raise MultiFrameError(
+                f"'{key}' is not an attribute name or tag"
+            ) from exc
+
+    return output
+
+
+def _key_values(attributes: Dataset, keys: list[BaseTag]) -> tuple[Any, ...]:
+    return tuple(
+        attributes[tag].value if tag in attributes else _MISSING for tag in keys
+    )
+
+
+def _compare_values(first: Any, second: Any) -> int:
+    if first is _MISSING:
+        return 0 if second is _MISSING else 1
+    if second is _MISSING:
+        return -1
+    if _values_equal(first, second):
+        return 0
+
+    try:
+        first_less = bool(first < second)
+        second_less = bool(second < first)
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError("Frame attribute values are not comparable") from exc
+
+    if first_less and not second_less:
+        return -1
+    if second_less and not first_less:
+        return 1
+    raise MultiFrameError("Frame attribute values are not comparable")
+
+
+def _compare_key_values(first: tuple[Any, ...], second: tuple[Any, ...]) -> int:
+    for first_value, second_value in zip(first, second):
+        result = _compare_values(first_value, second_value)
+        if result:
+            return result
+    return 0
+
+
+def _states_for_selection(
+    infos: list[_ValidatedDataset], selections: list[tuple[int, int]]
+) -> list[_FrameState]:
+    return [
+        _FrameState(
+            source=infos[source_index],
+            index=frame_index,
+            macros=_effective_macros(infos[source_index], frame_index),
+        )
+        for source_index, frame_index in selections
+    ]
+
+
+def _find_attribute(
+    state: _FrameState, tag: BaseTag
+) -> DataElement | None:
+    found: DataElement | None = None
+    for macro in state.macros.values():
+        item = macro.value[0]
+        if tag in item:
+            found = item[tag]
+    return found
+
+
+def _remove_attribute(state: _FrameState, tag: BaseTag) -> None:
+    for macro_tag in list(state.macros):
+        item = state.macros[macro_tag].value[0]
+        if tag in item:
+            del item[tag]
+        if len(item) == 0:
+            del state.macros[macro_tag]
+
+
+def _stack_key(states: list[_FrameState], state: _FrameState) -> Any:
+    element = _find_attribute(state, _STACK_ID)
+    return _MISSING if element is None else element.value
+
+
+def _renumber_in_stack_positions(states: list[_FrameState]) -> None:
+    stacks: list[tuple[Any, int]] = []
+    for state in states:
+        position = _find_attribute(state, _IN_STACK_POSITION_NUMBER)
+        if position is None:
+            continue
+
+        stack_value = _stack_key(states, state)
+        stack_index = None
+        for index, (known_value, next_position) in enumerate(stacks):
+            if _values_equal(known_value, stack_value):
+                stack_index = index
+                break
+
+        if stack_index is None:
+            stacks.append((stack_value, 2))
+            position.value = 1
+        else:
+            next_position = stacks[stack_index][1]
+            position.value = next_position
+            stacks[stack_index] = (stacks[stack_index][0], next_position + 1)
+
+
+def _dimension_values(element: DataElement | None) -> list[Any]:
+    if element is None or _is_empty(element.value):
+        return []
+    value = element.value
+    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
+        return list(value)
+    return [value]
+
+
+def _same_dimension_description(first: Dataset, second: Dataset) -> bool:
+    first_element = first.get(_DIMENSION_INDEX_SEQUENCE)
+    second_element = second.get(_DIMENSION_INDEX_SEQUENCE)
+    if (first_element is None) != (second_element is None):
+        return False
+    if first_element is None:
+        return True
+    return _values_equal(first_element.value, second_element.value)
+
+
+def _adjust_dimensions(
+    first: _ValidatedDataset, states: list[_FrameState]
+) -> tuple[bool, list[Dataset]]:
+    description_element = first.dataset.get(_DIMENSION_INDEX_SEQUENCE)
+    if description_element is None:
+        return False, []
+
+    try:
+        descriptions = list(description_element.value)
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError("Dimension Index Sequence is malformed") from exc
+    if not all(isinstance(item, Dataset) for item in descriptions):
+        _error("Dimension Index Sequence is malformed")
+
+    state_values = [
+        _dimension_values(_find_attribute(state, _DIMENSION_INDEX_VALUES))
+        for state in states
+    ]
+    if not any(state_values):
+        for state in states:
+            _remove_attribute(state, _DIMENSION_INDEX_VALUES)
+        return True, []
+
+    if any(len(values) > len(descriptions) for values in state_values):
+        _error("Dimension Index Values has more values than its description")
+
+    retained: list[int] = []
+    for dimension in range(len(descriptions)):
+        if all(len(values) > dimension for values in state_values):
+            first_value = state_values[0][dimension]
+            if all(
+                _values_equal(first_value, values[dimension])
+                for values in state_values[1:]
+            ):
+                continue
+        retained.append(dimension)
+
+    if not retained:
+        for state in states:
+            _remove_attribute(state, _DIMENSION_INDEX_VALUES)
+        return True, []
+
+    # Give each retained dimension its own compact, first-seen value space.
+    value_maps: dict[int, list[Any]] = {dimension: [] for dimension in retained}
+    for values in state_values:
+        for dimension in retained:
+            if dimension >= len(values):
+                continue
+            value = values[dimension]
+            known = value_maps[dimension]
+            if not any(_values_equal(value, item) for item in known):
+                known.append(value)
+
+    for state, values in zip(states, state_values):
+        element = _find_attribute(state, _DIMENSION_INDEX_VALUES)
+        if element is None:
+            continue
+        compact_values: list[int] = []
+        for dimension in retained:
+            if dimension >= len(values):
+                continue
+            known = value_maps[dimension]
+            compact_values.append(next(index for index, item in enumerate(known, 1) if _values_equal(item, values[dimension])))
+
+        if not compact_values:
+            _remove_attribute(state, _DIMENSION_INDEX_VALUES)
+        elif len(compact_values) == 1:
+            element.value = compact_values[0]
+        else:
+            element.value = compact_values
+
+    return True, [copy.deepcopy(descriptions[index]) for index in retained]
+
+
+def _consolidate_macros(states: list[_FrameState]) -> tuple[Dataset, list[Dataset]]:
+    all_tags: set[BaseTag] = set().union(*(set(state.macros) for state in states))
+    shared = Dataset()
+    per_frame = [Dataset() for _ in states]
+
+    for tag in sorted(all_tags):
+        present = [state.macros.get(tag) for state in states]
+        first = present[0]
+        is_shared = first is not None and all(element is not None for element in present)
+        if is_shared:
+            first_item = first.value[0]
+            is_shared = all(
+                _values_equal(first_item, element.value[0]) for element in present[1:]
+            )
+
+        if is_shared:
+            shared.add(_copy_macro(first))
+        else:
+            for dataset, element in zip(per_frame, present):
+                if element is not None:
+                    dataset.add(_copy_macro(element))
+
+    return shared, per_frame
+
+
+def _native_pixel_data(info: _ValidatedDataset, frames: list[bytes]) -> bytes:
+    if info.native_bits_allocated == 1:
+        if info.native_frame_pixels is None:
+            _error("Native Pixel Data has no frame shape")
+        try:
+            return concatenate_packed_frames(
+                frames,
+                frame_length=info.native_frame_pixels,
+                pad=True,
+            )
+        except Exception as exc:
+            raise MultiFrameError("Unable to rebuild native Pixel Data") from exc
+
+    data = b"".join(frames)
+    if len(data) % 2:
+        data += b"\x00"
+    return data
+
+
+def _set_dimension_description(
+    result: Dataset, first: _ValidatedDataset, has_description: bool, descriptions: list[Dataset]
+) -> None:
+    if not has_description:
+        return
+
+    if not descriptions:
+        if _DIMENSION_INDEX_SEQUENCE in result:
+            del result[_DIMENSION_INDEX_SEQUENCE]
+        return
+
+    element = copy.deepcopy(first.dataset[_DIMENSION_INDEX_SEQUENCE])
+    element.value = Sequence(descriptions)
+    result[_DIMENSION_INDEX_SEQUENCE] = element
+
+
+def _source_image_sequence(
+    result: Dataset,
+    infos: list[_ValidatedDataset],
+    selections: list[tuple[int, int]],
+) -> None:
+    frame_numbers: list[list[int]] = [[] for _ in infos]
+    for source_index, frame_index in selections:
+        frame_numbers[source_index].append(frame_index + 1)
+
+    sequence_items = []
+    for info, numbers in zip(infos, frame_numbers):
+        item = Dataset()
+        item[_REFERENCED_SOP_CLASS_UID] = DataElement(
+            _REFERENCED_SOP_CLASS_UID, "UI", copy.deepcopy(info.sop_class_uid)
+        )
+        item[_REFERENCED_SOP_INSTANCE_UID] = DataElement(
+            _REFERENCED_SOP_INSTANCE_UID, "UI", copy.deepcopy(info.sop_instance_uid)
+        )
+        item[_REFERENCED_FRAME_NUMBER] = DataElement(
+            _REFERENCED_FRAME_NUMBER, "IS", copy.deepcopy(numbers)
+        )
+        sequence_items.append(item)
+
+    result[_SOURCE_IMAGE_SEQUENCE] = DataElement(
+        _SOURCE_IMAGE_SEQUENCE, "SQ", Sequence(sequence_items)
+    )
+
+
+def _derive(
+    infos: list[_ValidatedDataset], selections: list[tuple[int, int]]
+) -> Dataset:
+    if not selections:
+        _error("At least one frame must be selected")
+
+    first = infos[0]
+    states = _states_for_selection(infos, selections)
+    _renumber_in_stack_positions(states)
+    has_dimension_description, descriptions = _adjust_dimensions(first, states)
+    shared, per_frame = _consolidate_macros(states)
+
+    result = copy.deepcopy(first.dataset)
+    result.NumberOfFrames = len(selections)
+    result.SharedFunctionalGroupsSequence = Sequence([shared])
+    result.PerFrameFunctionalGroupsSequence = Sequence(per_frame)
+    _set_dimension_description(result, first, has_dimension_description, descriptions)
+
+    selected_frames = [
+        info.frames[frame_index]
+        for source_index, frame_index in selections
+        for info in (infos[source_index],)
+    ]
+    if first.encapsulated:
+        pixel_data = encapsulate(selected_frames)
+        result[first.pixel_tag].value = pixel_data
+        result[first.pixel_tag].VR = "OB"
+        result[first.pixel_tag].is_undefined_length = True
+    else:
+        result[first.pixel_tag].value = _native_pixel_data(first, selected_frames)
+        result[first.pixel_tag].is_undefined_length = False
+
+    for tag in (_EXTENDED_OFFSET_TABLE, _EXTENDED_OFFSET_TABLE_LENGTHS):
+        if tag in result:
+            del result[tag]
+
+    _source_image_sequence(result, infos, selections)
+
+    new_instance_uid = generate_uid()
+    result.SOPInstanceUID = new_instance_uid
+    result.ensure_file_meta()
+    result.file_meta.MediaStorageSOPClassUID = copy.deepcopy(result.SOPClassUID)
+    result.file_meta.MediaStorageSOPInstanceUID = new_instance_uid
+    return result
+
+
+def _check_combinable(infos: list[_ValidatedDataset]) -> None:
+    if not infos:
+        _error("merge_frames requires one or more datasets")
+
+    first = infos[0]
+    for index, info in enumerate(infos[1:], 1):
+        if not _values_equal(first.sop_class_uid, info.sop_class_uid):
+            _error(f"Dataset {index} has a different SOP Class UID")
+        if first.transfer_syntax != info.transfer_syntax:
+            _error(f"Dataset {index} has a different Transfer Syntax UID")
+        if first.pixel_tag != info.pixel_tag or first.pixel_vr != info.pixel_vr:
+            _error(f"Dataset {index} has a different pixel data element")
+
+        for tag in _IMAGE_PIXEL_ATTRIBUTES:
+            first_element = first.dataset.get(tag)
+            second_element = info.dataset.get(tag)
+            if (first_element is None) != (second_element is None):
+                _error(f"Dataset {index} has different image pixel attributes")
+            if first_element is not None and not _values_equal(
+                first_element.value, second_element.value
+            ):
+                _error(f"Dataset {index} has different image pixel attributes")
+
+        if not _same_dimension_description(first.dataset, info.dataset):
+            _error(f"Dataset {index} has a different Dimension Index Sequence")
+
+
+def extract_frames(ds: Dataset, indices: Iterable[int]) -> Dataset:
+    """Return a derived instance containing the selected frames in order."""
+
+    info = _validate_dataset(ds)
+    try:
+        raw_indices = list(indices)

[project]

]
classifiers=[
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Intended Audience :: Healthcare Industry",
    "Intended Audience :: Science/Research",
    "Development Status :: 5 - Production/Stable",
    "Programming Language :: Python",

    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",

    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Physics",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries"

description = "A pure Python package for reading and writing DICOM data"

keywords = ["dicom", "python", "medical", "imaging"]

license-files = ["LICENSE"]
name = "pydicom"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10"

[project.optional-dependencies]

[project.scripts]

class PrivateBlock:
    """Helper class for a private block in the :class:`Dataset`.

    See the DICOM Standard, Part 5,
    :dcm:`Section 7.8.1<part05/sect_7.8.html#sect_7.8.1>` - Private Data
    Element Tags

    Attributes
    ----------
    group : int
        The private group where the private block is located as a 32-bit
        :class:`int`.
    private_creator : str
        The private creator string related to the block.
    dataset : Dataset
        The parent dataset.
    block_start : int
        The start element of the private block as a 32-bit :class:`int`. Note
        that the 2 low order hex digits of the element are always 0.
    """

    def __init__(
        self, key: tuple[int, str], dataset: "Dataset", private_creator_element: int
    ) -> None:
        """Initializes an object corresponding to a private tag block.

        Parameters
        ----------
        key : tuple
            The private (tag group, creator) as ``(int, str)``. The group
            must be an odd number.
        dataset : Dataset
            The parent :class:`Dataset`.
        private_creator_element : int
            The element of the private creator tag as a 32-bit :class:`int`.
        """
        self.group = key[0]
        self.private_creator = key[1]
        self.dataset = dataset
        self.block_start = private_creator_element << 8

    def get_tag(self, element_offset: int) -> BaseTag:
        """Return the private tag ID for the given `element_offset`.

        Parameters
        ----------
        element_offset : int
            The lower 16 bits (e.g. 2 hex numbers) of the element tag.

        Returns
        -------
            The tag ID defined by the private block location and the
            given element offset.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If `element_offset` is too large.
        """
        if element_offset > 0xFF:
            raise ValueError("Element offset must be less than 256")
        return Tag(self.group, self.block_start + element_offset)

    def __contains__(self, element_offset: int) -> bool:
        """Return ``True`` if the tag with given `element_offset` is in
        the parent :class:`Dataset`.
        """
        return self.get_tag(element_offset) in self.dataset

    def __getitem__(self, element_offset: int) -> DataElement:
        """Return the data element in the parent dataset for the given element
        offset.

        Parameters
        ----------
        element_offset : int
            The lower 16 bits (e.g. 2 hex numbers) of the element tag.

        Returns
        -------
            The data element of the tag in the parent dataset defined by the
            private block location and the given element offset.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If `element_offset` is too large.
        KeyError
            If no data element exists at that offset.
        """
        return self.dataset.__getitem__(self.get_tag(element_offset))

    def __delitem__(self, element_offset: int) -> None:
        """Delete the tag with the given `element_offset` from the dataset.

        Parameters
        ----------
        element_offset : int
            The lower 16 bits (e.g. 2 hex numbers) of the element tag
            to be deleted.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If `element_offset` is too large.
        KeyError
            If no data element exists at that offset.
        """
        del self.dataset[self.get_tag(element_offset)]

    def add_new(self, element_offset: int, VR: str, value: object) -> None:
        """Add a private element to the parent :class:`Dataset`.

        Adds the private tag with the given `VR` and `value` to the parent
        :class:`Dataset` at the tag ID defined by the private block and the
        given `element_offset`.

        Parameters
        ----------
        element_offset : int
            The lower 16 bits (e.g. 2 hex numbers) of the element tag
            to be added.
        VR : str
            The 2 character DICOM value representation.
        value
            The value of the data element. See :meth:`Dataset.add_new()`
            for a description.
        """
        tag = self.get_tag(element_offset)
        self.dataset.add_new(tag, VR, value)
        self.dataset[tag].private_creator = self.private_creator


def _dict_equal(a: "Dataset", b: Any, exclude: list[str] | None = None) -> bool:
    """Common method for Dataset.__eq__ and FileDataset.__eq__

    Uses .keys() as needed because Dataset iter return items not keys
    `exclude` is used in FileDataset__eq__ ds.__dict__ compare, which
    would also compare the wrapped _dict member (entire dataset) again.
    """
    return (
        len(a) == len(b)
        and all(key in b for key in a.keys())
        and all(
            a[key] == b[key]
            for key in a.keys()
            if exclude is None or key not in exclude
        )
    )

def parse_basic_offsets(
    buffer: bytes | bytearray | ReadableBuffer, *, endianness: str = "<"
) -> list[int]:
    """Return the encapsulated pixel data's basic offset table frame offsets.

    .. versionadded:: 3.0

    Parameters
    ----------
    buffer : bytes | bytearray | readable buffer
        A buffer containing the encapsulated frame data, positioned at the
        beginning of the Basic Offset Table. May be :class:`bytes`,
        :class:`bytearray` or an object with ``read()``, ``tell()`` and
        ``seek()`` methods. If the latter then after reading it will be
        positioned at the start of the item tag of the first fragment after the
        Basic Offset Table.
    endianness : str, optional
        If ``"<"`` (default) then the encapsulated data uses little endian
        encoding, otherwise if ``">"`` it uses big endian encoding.

    Returns
    -------
    list[int]
        A list of the offset positions to the first item tag of each frame, as
        measured from the end of the basic offset table.

    References
    ----------
    :dcm:`DICOM Standard, Part 5, Annex A.4<part05/sect_A.4.html#table_A.4-1>`
    """
    if isinstance(buffer, bytes | bytearray):
        buffer = BytesIO(buffer)

    group, elem = unpack(f"{endianness}HH", buffer.read(4))
    if group << 16 | elem != 0xFFFEE000:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Found unexpected tag {Tag(group, elem)} instead of (FFFE,E000) "
            "when parsing the Basic Offset Table item"
        )

    length = unpack(f"{endianness}L", buffer.read(4))[0]
    if length % 4:
        raise ValueError(
            "The length of the Basic Offset Table item is not a multiple of 4"
        )

    if length == 0:
        return []

    return list(unpack(f"{endianness}{length // 4}L", buffer.read(length)))

    if isinstance(arg, tuple | list):
        if len(arg) != 2:
            raise ValueError("Tag must be an int or a 2-tuple")

        valid = False
        if isinstance(arg[0], str):
            valid = isinstance(arg[1], str)
            if valid:
                arg = (int(arg[0], 16), int(arg[1], 16))
        elif isinstance(arg[0], int):
            valid = isinstance(arg[1], int)
        if not valid:
            raise TypeError(
                f"Unable to create an element tag from '{arg}': both "
                "arguments must be the same type and str or int"
            )

        if arg[0] > 0xFFFF or arg[1] > 0xFFFF:
            raise OverflowError(
                f"Unable to create an element tag from '{arg}': the group "
                "and element values are limited to a maximum of 2-bytes each"
            )

        long_value = (arg[0] << 16) | arg[1]

    # Single str parameter
    elif isinstance(arg, str):
        try:
            long_value = int(arg, 16)
            if long_value > 0xFFFFFFFF:
                raise OverflowError(
                    f"Unable to create an element tag from '{long_value}': "
                    "the combined group and element values  are limited to a "
                    "maximum of 4-bytes"
                )
        except ValueError:
            # Try a DICOM keyword
            from pydicom.datadict import tag_for_keyword

            long_value = tag_for_keyword(arg)
            if long_value is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Unable to create an element tag from '{arg}': "
                    "unknown DICOM element keyword or an invalid int"
                )
    # Single int parameter
    else:
        long_value = arg
        if long_value > 0xFFFFFFFF:
            raise OverflowError(
                f"Unable to create an element tag from '{long_value}': the "
                "combined group and element values are limited to a maximum "
                "of 4-bytes"
            )

    if long_value < 0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unable to create an element tag from '{long_value}': tags must "
            "be positive"
        )

    return BaseTag(long_value)


class BaseTag(int):
    """Represents a DICOM element (group, element) tag.

    Tags are represented as an :class:`int`.
    """

    # Override comparisons so can convert "other" to Tag as necessary
    #   See Ordering Comparisons at:
    #   https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.0.html#ordering-comparisons
    def __le__(self, other: Any) -> Any:
        """Return ``True`` if `self`  is less than or equal to `other`."""
        return self == other or self < other

    def __lt__(self, other: Any) -> Any:
        """Return ``True`` if `self` is less than `other`."""
        # Check if comparing with another Tag object; if not, create a temp one
        if not isinstance(other, int):
            try:
                other = Tag(other)
            except Exception:
                raise TypeError("Cannot compare Tag with non-Tag item")

        return int(self) < int(other)

    def __ge__(self, other: Any) -> Any:
        """Return ``True`` if `self` is greater than or equal to `other`."""
        return self == other or self > other

    def __gt__(self, other: Any) -> Any:
        """Return ``True`` if `self` is greater than `other`."""
        return not (self == other or self < other)

    def __eq__(self, other: Any) -> Any:
        """Return ``True`` if `self` equals `other`."""
        # Check if comparing with another Tag object; if not, create a temp one
        if not isinstance(other, int):
            try:
                other = Tag(other)
            except Exception:
                return False

        return int(self) == int(other)

    def __ne__(self, other: Any) -> Any:
        """Return ``True`` if `self` does not equal `other`."""
        return not self == other

    # For python 3, any override of __cmp__ or __eq__
    # immutable requires explicit redirect of hash function
    # to the parent class
    #   See https://docs.python.org/3/reference/datamodel.html#object.__hash__
    __hash__ = int.__hash__

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        """Return the tag value as a hex string '(gggg,eeee)'."""
        return f"({self.group:04X},{self.element:04X})"

    __repr__ = __str__

    @property
    def json_key(self) -> str:
        """Return the tag value as a JSON key string 'GGGGEEEE'."""
        return f"{self.group:04X}{self.element:04X}"

    @property
    def group(self) -> int:
        """Return the tag's group number as :class:`int`."""
        return self >> 16

    @property
    def element(self) -> int:
        """Return the tag's element number as :class:`int`."""
        return self & 0xFFFF

    elem = element  # alternate syntax

    @property
    def is_private(self) -> bool:
        """Return ``True`` if the tag is private (has an odd group number)."""
        return self.group % 2 == 1

    @property
    def is_private_creator(self) -> bool:
        """Return ``True`` if the tag is a private creator."""
        return self.is_private and 0x0010 <= self.element < 0x0100

    @property
    def private_creator(self) -> "BaseTag":
        """Return the private creator tag for the given tag.
        The result is meaningless if this is not a private tag.

        .. versionadded:: 2.4
        """
        return BaseTag((self & 0xFFFF0000) | self.element >> 8)

"""Functions for handling DICOM unique identifiers (UIDs)"""

import hashlib
from keyword import iskeyword
import re
import secrets
import uuid

from pydicom import config
from pydicom._uid_dict import UID_dictionary
from pydicom.config import disable_value_validation
from pydicom.valuerep import STR_VR_REGEXES, validate_value


class UID(str):
    """Human friendly UIDs as a Python :class:`str` subclass.

    **Private Transfer Syntaxes**

    If creating a private transfer syntax UID, then you must also use
    :meth:`~pydicom.UID.set_private_encoding` to set the corresponding
    dataset encoding.

    Examples
    --------

    General usage::

      >>> from pydicom.uid import UID
      >>> uid = UID('1.2.840.10008.1.2.4.50')
      >>> uid
      '1.2.840.10008.1.2.4.50'
      >>> uid.is_implicit_VR
      False
      >>> uid.is_little_endian
      True
      >>> uid.is_transfer_syntax
      True
      >>> uid.name
      'JPEG Baseline (Process 1)'
      >>> uid.keyword
      JPEGBaseline8Bit

    Setting the encoding to explicit VR little endian for a private transfer
    syntax::

      >>> uid = UID("1.2.3.4")
      >>> uid.set_private_encoding(False, True)

    """

    _PRIVATE_TS_ENCODING: tuple[bool, bool]
    _NATIVE_ENCODING = [
        "1.2.840.10008.1.2",  # Explicit VR Little Endian
        "1.2.840.10008.1.2.1",  # Implicit VR Little Endian
        "1.2.840.10008.1.2.2",  # Explicit VR Big Endian
        "1.2.840.10008.1.2.1.99",  # Deflated Explicit VR Little Endian
    ]

    def __new__(
        cls: type["UID"], val: str, validation_mode: int | None = None
    ) -> "UID":
        """Setup new instance of the class.

        Parameters
        ----------
        val : str or pydicom.uid.UID
            The UID string to use to create the UID object.
        validation_mode : int
            Defines if values are validated and how validation errors are
            handled.

        Returns
        -------
        pydicom.uid.UID
            The UID object.
        """
        if isinstance(val, str):
            if validation_mode is None:
                validation_mode = config.settings.reading_validation_mode
            validate_value("UI", val, validation_mode)

            uid = super().__new__(cls, val.strip())
            if hasattr(val, "_PRIVATE_TS_ENCODING"):
                uid._PRIVATE_TS_ENCODING = val._PRIVATE_TS_ENCODING

            return uid

        raise TypeError("A UID must be created from a string")

    @property
    def is_implicit_VR(self) -> bool:
        """Return ``True`` if an implicit VR transfer syntax UID."""
        if self.is_transfer_syntax:
            if not self.is_private:
                # Implicit VR Little Endian
                if self == "1.2.840.10008.1.2":
                    return True

                # Explicit VR Little Endian
                # Explicit VR Big Endian
                # Deflated Explicit VR Little Endian
                # All encapsulated transfer syntaxes
                return False

            return self._PRIVATE_TS_ENCODING[0]

        raise ValueError("UID is not a transfer syntax.")

    @property
    def is_little_endian(self) -> bool:
        """Return ``True`` if a little endian transfer syntax UID."""
        if self.is_transfer_syntax:
            if not self.is_private:
                # Explicit VR Big Endian
                if self == "1.2.840.10008.1.2.2":
                    return False

                # Explicit VR Little Endian
                # Implicit VR Little Endian
                # Deflated Explicit VR Little Endian
                # All encapsulated transfer syntaxes
                return True

            return self._PRIVATE_TS_ENCODING[1]

        raise ValueError("UID is not a transfer syntax.")

    @property
    def is_transfer_syntax(self) -> bool:
        """Return ``True`` if a transfer syntax UID."""
        if not self.is_private:
            return self.type == "Transfer Syntax"

        return hasattr(self, "_PRIVATE_TS_ENCODING")

    @property
    def is_deflated(self) -> bool:
        """Return ``True`` if a deflated transfer syntax UID."""
        if self.is_transfer_syntax:
            # Deflated Explicit VR Little Endian
            if self == "1.2.840.10008.1.2.1.99":
                return True

            # Explicit VR Little Endian
            # Implicit VR Little Endian
            # Explicit VR Big Endian
            # All encapsulated transfer syntaxes
            return False

        raise ValueError("UID is not a transfer syntax.")

    @property
    def is_encapsulated(self) -> bool:
        """Return ``True`` if an encasulated transfer syntax UID."""
        return self.is_compressed

    @property
    def is_compressed(self) -> bool:
        """Return ``True`` if a compressed transfer syntax UID."""
        if self.is_transfer_syntax:
            if self in self._NATIVE_ENCODING:
                return False

            # All encapsulated transfer syntaxes
            return True

        raise ValueError("UID is not a transfer syntax.")

    @property
    def keyword(self) -> str:
        """Return the UID keyword from the UID dictionary."""
        if str(self) in UID_dictionary:
            return UID_dictionary[self][4]

        return ""

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        """Return the UID name from the UID dictionary."""
        uid_string = str(self)
        if uid_string in UID_dictionary:
            return UID_dictionary[self][0]

        return uid_string

    @property
    def type(self) -> str:
        """Return the UID type from the UID dictionary."""
        if str(self) in UID_dictionary:
            return UID_dictionary[self][1]

        return ""

    @property
    def info(self) -> str:
        """Return the UID info from the UID dictionary."""
        if str(self) in UID_dictionary:
            return UID_dictionary[self][2]

        return ""

    @property
    def is_retired(self) -> bool:
        """Return ``True`` if the UID is retired, ``False`` otherwise or if
        private.
        """
        if str(self) in UID_dictionary:
            return bool(UID_dictionary[self][3])

        return False

    @property
    def is_private(self) -> bool:
        """Return ``True`` if the UID isn't an officially registered DICOM
        UID.
        """
        return not self.startswith("1.2.840.10008.")

"""Define the Sequence class, which contains a sequence DataElement's items.

Sequence is a list of pydicom Dataset objects.
"""

from typing import cast, Any, TypeVar
from collections.abc import Iterable

from pydicom.dataset import Dataset
from pydicom.multival import ConstrainedList


# Python 3.11 adds typing.Self, until then...
Self = TypeVar("Self", bound="Sequence")


class Sequence(ConstrainedList[Dataset]):
    """Class to hold multiple :class:`~pydicom.dataset.Dataset` in a :class:`list`."""

    def __init__(self, iterable: Iterable[Dataset] | None = None) -> None:
        """Initialize a list of :class:`~pydicom.dataset.Dataset`.

        Parameters
        ----------
        iterable : Iterable[Dataset] | None
            An iterable object (e.g. :class:`list`, :class:`tuple`) containing
            :class:`~pydicom.dataset.Dataset`. If not used then an empty
            :class:`Sequence` is generated.
        """
        # We add this extra check to throw a relevant error. Without it, the
        # error will be simply that a Sequence must contain Datasets (since a
        # Dataset IS iterable). This error, however, doesn't inform the user
        # that the actual issue is that their Dataset needs to be INSIDE an
        # iterable object
        if isinstance(iterable, Dataset):
            raise TypeError("The Sequence constructor requires an iterable")

        # If True, SQ element uses an undefined length of 0xFFFFFFFF
        self.is_undefined_length: bool

        super().__init__(iterable)

    def extend(self, val: Iterable[Dataset]) -> None:
        """Extend the :class:`~pydicom.sequence.Sequence` using an iterable
        of :class:`~pydicom.dataset.Dataset` instances.
        """
        if isinstance(val, Dataset):
            raise TypeError("An iterable of 'Dataset' is required")

        super().extend(val)

    def __iadd__(self: Self, other: Iterable[Dataset]) -> Self:
        """Implement Sequence() += [Dataset()]."""
        if isinstance(other, Dataset):
            raise TypeError("An iterable of 'Dataset' is required")

        return super().__iadd__(other)

    def __setitem__(self, index: slice | int, val: Iterable[Dataset] | Dataset) -> None:
        """Add item(s) to the Sequence at `index`."""
        if isinstance(index, slice):
            if isinstance(val, Dataset):
                raise TypeError("Can only assign an iterable of 'Dataset'")

            super().__setitem__(index, val)
        else:
            super().__setitem__(index, cast(Dataset, val))

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        """String description of the Sequence."""
        return f"[{''.join([str(x) for x in self])}]"

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        """String representation of the Sequence."""
        return f"<{self.__class__.__name__}, length {len(self)}>"

    @staticmethod
    def _validate(item: Any) -> Dataset:
        """Check that `item` is a :class:`~pydicom.dataset.Dataset` instance."""
        if isinstance(item, Dataset):
            return item

        raise TypeError("Sequence contents must be 'Dataset' instances.")

def parse_fragments(
    buffer: bytes | bytearray | ReadableBuffer, *, endianness: str = "<"
) -> tuple[int, list[int]]:
    """Return the number of fragments and their positions in `buffer`.

    .. versionadded:: 3.0

    Parameters
    ----------
    buffer : bytes | bytearray | readable buffer
        A buffer containing the encapsulated frame data, starting at the first
        byte of item tag for a fragment, such as after the end of the Basic
        Basic Offset Table. May be :class:`bytes`, :class:`bytearray` or an
        object with ``read()``, ``tell()`` and ``seek()`` methods. If the latter
        then the offset will be reset to the starting position afterwards.
    endianness : str, optional
        If ``"<"`` (default) then the encapsulated data uses little endian
        encoding, otherwise if ``">"`` it uses big endian encoding.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[int, list[int]]
        The number of fragments and the absolute offset position of the first
        byte of the item tag for each fragment in `buffer`.
    """
    if isinstance(buffer, bytes | bytearray):
        buffer = BytesIO(buffer)

    start_offset = buffer.tell()

    nr_fragments = 0
    fragment_offsets = []
    while True:
        try:
            group, elem = unpack(f"{endianness}HH", buffer.read(4))
        except Exception:
            break

        tag = group << 16 | elem
        if tag == 0xFFFEE000:
            if len(raw_length := buffer.read(4)) != 4:
                raise ValueError(
                    "Unable to determine the length of the item at offset "
                    f"{buffer.tell() - len(raw_length) - 4} as the end of "
                    "the data has been reached - the encapsulated pixel data "
                    "may be invalid"
                )
            length = unpack(f"{endianness}L", raw_length)[0]
            if length == 0xFFFFFFFF:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Undefined item length at offset {buffer.tell() - 4} when "
                    "parsing the encapsulated pixel data fragments"
                )
            nr_fragments += 1
            fragment_offsets.append(buffer.tell() - 8)
            buffer.seek(length, 1)
        elif tag == 0xFFFEE0DD:
            break
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unexpected tag '{Tag(tag)}' at offset {buffer.tell() - 4} when "
                "parsing the encapsulated pixel data fragment items"
            )

    buffer.seek(start_offset, 0)

    return nr_fragments, fragment_offsets


def generate_fragments(
    buffer: bytes | bytearray | ReadableBuffer, *, endianness: str = "<"
) -> Iterator[bytes]:
    """Yield frame fragments from the encapsulated pixel data in `buffer`.

    .. versionadded:: 3.0

    Parameters
    ----------
    buffer : bytes | bytearray | readable buffer
        A buffer containing the encapsulated frame data, starting at the first
        byte of item tag for a fragment, usually this will be after the end
        of the Basic Offset Table. May be :class:`bytes`, :class:`bytearray` or
        an object with ``read()``, ``tell()`` and ``seek()`` methods. If the
        latter than the final offset position depends on how many fragments have
        been yielded.
    endianness : str, optional
        If ``"<"`` (default) then the encapsulated data uses little endian
        encoding, otherwise if ``">"`` it uses big endian encoding.

    Yields
    ------
    bytes
        A pixel data fragment.
    """
    if isinstance(buffer, bytes | bytearray):
        buffer = BytesIO(buffer)

    while True:
        try:
            group, elem = unpack(f"{endianness}HH", buffer.read(4))
        except Exception:
            break

        tag = group << 16 | elem
        if tag == 0xFFFEE000:
            if len(raw_length := buffer.read(4)) != 4:
                raise ValueError(
                    "Unable to determine the length of the item at offset "
                    f"{buffer.tell() - len(raw_length) - 4} as the end of "
                    "the data has been reached - the encapsulated pixel data "
                    "may be invalid"
                )
            length = unpack(f"{endianness}L", raw_length)[0]
            if length == 0xFFFFFFFF:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Undefined item length at offset {buffer.tell() - 4} when "
                    "parsing the encapsulated pixel data fragments"
                )

            yield buffer.read(length)
        elif tag == 0xFFFEE0DD:
            break
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unexpected tag '{Tag(tag)}' at offset {buffer.tell() - 4} when "
                "parsing the encapsulated pixel data fragment items"
            )


def generate_fragmented_frames(
    buffer: bytes | bytearray | ReadableBuffer,
    *,
    number_of_frames: int | None = None,
    extended_offsets: tuple[list[int], list[int]] | tuple[bytes, bytes] | None = None,
    endianness: str = "<",
) -> Iterator[tuple[bytes, ...]]:
    """Yield fragmented pixel data frames from `buffer`.

    .. versionadded:: 3.0

    .. note::

        When the Basic Offset Table is empty and the Extended Offset Table
        isn't supplied then more fragmented frames may be yielded than given
        by `number_of_frames` provided there are sufficient excess fragments
        available.

    Parameters
    ----------
    buffer : bytes | bytearray | readable buffer
        A buffer containing the encapsulated frame data, positioned at the first
        byte of the basic offset table. May be :class:`bytes`,
        :class:`bytearray` or an object with ``read()``, ``tell()`` and
        ``seek()`` methods. If the latter then the final position depends on
        how many fragmented frames have been yielded.
    number_of_frames : int, optional
        Required when the Basic Offset Table is empty and the Extended Offset Table
        has not been supplied. This should be the value of (0028,0008) *Number of
        Frames* or the expected number of frames in the encapsulated data.
    extended_offsets : tuple[list[int], list[int]] or tuple[bytes, bytes], optional
        The (offsets, lengths) of the Extended Offset Table as taken from
        (7FE0,0001) *Extended Offset Table* and (7FE0,0002) *Extended Offset
        Table Lengths* as either the raw encoded values or a list of their
        decoded equivalents.
    endianness : str, optional
        If ``"<"`` (default) then the encapsulated data uses little endian
        encoding, otherwise if ``">"`` it uses big endian encoding.

    Yields
    -------
    tuple[bytes, ...]
        An encapsulated pixel data frame, with the contents of the tuple the
        frame's fragmented encoded data.
    """
    if isinstance(buffer, bytes | bytearray):
        buffer = BytesIO(buffer)

    basic_offsets = parse_basic_offsets(buffer, endianness=endianness)
    # `buffer` is positioned at the end of the basic offsets table

    # Prefer the extended offset table (if available)
    if extended_offsets:
        # PS3.3, C.7.6.3.1.8
        # Byte offsets to the first byte of the item tag of the first fragment
        #   of every frame, as measured from the first byte of the item tag
        #   following the Basic Offset Table, which *should* be empty
        # Only 1 fragment per frame is allowed (Table C.7-11a)
        if isinstance(extended_offsets[0], bytes):
            nr_offsets = len(extended_offsets[0]) // 8
            offsets = list(unpack(f"{endianness}{nr_offsets}Q", extended_offsets[0]))
        else:
            offsets = extended_offsets[0]

        if isinstance(extended_offsets[1], bytes):
            nr_offsets = len(extended_offsets[1]) // 8
            lengths = list(unpack(f"{endianness}{nr_offsets}Q", extended_offsets[1]))
        else:
            lengths = extended_offsets[1]

        fragments_start = buffer.tell()
        for offset, length in zip(offsets, lengths):
            # 8 for the item tag and item length, which we don't need
            buffer.seek(fragments_start + offset + 8, 0)
            yield (buffer.read(length),)

        return

    # Fall back to the basic offset table (if available)
    if basic_offsets:
        frame = []
        current_index = 0
        current_offset = 0
        final_index = len(basic_offsets) - 1
        for fragment in generate_fragments(buffer, endianness=endianness):
            if current_index == final_index:
                # Nth frame, keep adding fragments until we have no more
                frame.append(fragment)
                continue

            if current_offset < basic_offsets[current_index + 1]:
                # N - 1th frame, keep adding fragments until the we go
                #   past the next frame offset
                frame.append(fragment)
            else:
                # Gone past the next offset, yield and restart
                yield tuple(frame)
                current_index += 1
                frame = [fragment]

            # + 8 bytes for item tag and item length
            current_offset += len(fragment) + 8

        # Yield the Nth frame
        yield tuple(frame)
        return

    # No basic or extended offset table
    # Determine the number of fragments in the buffer
    nr_fragments, _ = parse_fragments(buffer, endianness=endianness)
    # `buffer` is positioned at the end of the basic offsets table
    fragments = generate_fragments(buffer, endianness=endianness)

    # Single fragment must be 1 frame
    if nr_fragments == 1:
        yield (next(fragments),)
        return

    # From this point on we require the number of frames as there are
    #   multiple fragments and may be one or more frames
    if not number_of_frames:
        raise ValueError(
            "Unable to determine the frame boundaries for the encapsulated "
            "pixel data as there is no Basic or Extended Offset Table and "
            "the number of frames has not been supplied"
        )

    # 1 fragment per frame, for N frames
    if nr_fragments == number_of_frames:
        # Covers RLE and others if 1:1 ratio
        yield from ((fragment,) for fragment in fragments)
        return

    # Multiple fragments for 1 frame
    if number_of_frames == 1:
        yield tuple(fragment for fragment in fragments)
        return

    # More fragments then frames
    if nr_fragments > number_of_frames:
        # Search for JPEG/JPEG-LS/JPEG2K EOI/EOC marker which should be the
        #   last two bytes of a frame
        # It's possible to yield more frames than `number_of_frames` as
        #   long as there are excess fragments with JPEG EOI/EOC markers
        # It's also possible that we yielded too early because the marker bytes
        #   were actually part of the compressed JPEG codestream
        eoi_marker = b"\xff\xd9"
        frame = []
        frame_nr = 0
        for fragment in fragments:
            frame.append(fragment)
            if eoi_marker in fragment[-10:]:
                yield tuple(frame)
                frame_nr += 1
                frame = []

        # There was a final set of fragments with no EOI/EOC marker, data is
        #   probably corrupted, but yield it and warn/log anyway
        if frame:
            if frame_nr >= number_of_frames:
                msg = (
                    "The end of the encapsulated pixel data has been reached but "
                    "no JPEG EOI/EOC marker was found, the final frame may be "
                    "be invalid"
                )
            else:
                msg = (
                    "The end of the encapsulated pixel data has been reached but "
                    "fewer frames than expected have been found. Please confirm "
                    "that the generated frame data is correct"
                )

            warn_and_log(msg)
            yield tuple(frame)

        elif frame_nr < number_of_frames:
            warn_and_log(
                "The end of the encapsulated pixel data has been reached but "
                "fewer frames than expected have been found"
            )

        return

    # nr_fragments < number_of_frames
    raise ValueError(
        "Unable to generate frames from the encapsulated pixel data as there "
        "are fewer fragments than frames; the dataset may be corrupt or the "
        "number of frames may be incorrect"
